images.note: Engraved title page of de Bry's 1614 Latin edition of Las Casas's Short Account (Narratio regionum Indicarum): Spaniards receiving tribute goods from Native bearers — the encomienda's labor-and-tribute grant made visual. European imagination (de Bry never crossed the Atlantic), not documentary.
images.source: Getty Research Institute (scan via Internet Archive)
images.title: Encomienda tribute — engraved title page, de Bry's Latin Short Account (1614)

images.note: Bartolome de Las Casas as painted by Constantino Brumidi in the U.S. Capitol (19th century — later depiction, not contemporary). Covers his encomienda renunciation (1514), New Laws lobbying, Short Account at court, 1516 African-labor proposal and retraction.
images.title: Bartolome de Las Casas — Brumidi fresco, U.S. Capitol (19th c.)

images.note: 1791 printed plan of the slave ship Brookes (from 1788 measurements): deck plans and cross-sections showing legal stowage of captives — the Middle Passage's 'priced-in' 13% mortality made visual. Later British abolitionist print, not a contemporary Spanish vessel.
images.title: Plan of the slave ship Brookes (1791)
